newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds slide, track overseas weakness.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds slide, track overseas weakness.

text.p: Irish bonds were traded down on Wednesday, tracking a general slide in overseas bond markets following a rise in the U.S. federal fund rate, dealers said.
"Most of the trade flow today has been switch-related, with investors moving into longer-yield bonds," a dealer said. "Price-wise we're reversing the up-trade of yesterday."

On Tuesday Irish bonds performed well across the yield curve ahead of the conclusion of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Open Market Committee Meeting, which saw a 25 basis points rise in rates.
The quarter percent increase has been widely expected and factored in by markets in advance.
"So far today there's no change in the Irish spread against bunds," the dealer said. "The 10-year bond is more or less unchanged at 98 basis points over Germany."
Dealers said the market would be watching all data out of the U.S. as an indication of further rate increases.
"If the data's strong the Fed may want to slow things down with a further rise, so strong data is generally not good for bond markets."
Payroll and NAPM figures are expected next week.
Dealers said there was a brief flurry of activity earlier in the day on the back of a stronger-than-expected increase in U.S. orders for durable goods.
The long Easter weekend -- with Dublin markets closed on Friday and Monday -- would probably damp trading activity through the rest of the week, dealers said.

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 23 pence from Tuesday's close at 101.17 to yield 6.18 percent while the benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down 27 pence from the close at 107.53 to yield 6.88 percent.
